learning_outcomes.text: assess the technical-economic viability of an industrial investment
develop the sizing of a production plant
use the main project management techniques to manage the main phases of plant construction
define the best equipment layout with respect to the kind of product manufactured and production volumes forecast
identify the correct holding techniques in specific manufacturing environments
use the main techniques for time and work study
decide on the use of the best maintenance techniques with respect to company equipment

carry out the sizing of the plant main auxiliary systems (heating system, electrical system, combined heat and power generation; industrial water supply and distribution; fire-fighting systems; production and distribution of compressed air)

syllabus_topics: Introduction to industrial manufacturing: structure of manufacturing systems and classification criteria for industrial enterprises; the manufacturing system in the industrial enterprise
Development of an industrial initiative: market analysis; production capacity sizing; plant location
Feasibility Study: technical - economic - financial assessments; profitability indexes (PBP, NPV, DCFRR); investment risk analysis
Manufacturing system design: plant layout; continuous and batch production; Economic Production Quantity; sizing of the means of production; queuing theory
Project planning: program evaluation techniques and their use in the design, construction and operation of industrial plants (PERT and CPM)

Work measurement and organization: Taylor and the principles of scientific management; Methods and Time Measurement; stopwatch time study; predetermined times methods (Work Factor, MTM); work sampling; manpower sizing; Design for Manufacturing and Assembly
Inventory management: raw materials and finished goods storage; Economic Order Quantity; quantity discounts; techniques of inventory management; safety stock
Reliability: fundamentals; components and systems reliability; Fault Tree Analysis
Plant maintenance: maintenance policies (fault maintenance, preventive maintenance, predictive maintenance); Total Productive Maintenance

Auxiliary systems: piping; Hardy Cross method; industrial water supply and distribution; fire-fighting system; heating system; electrical system; Combined Heat and Power generation; production and distribution of compressed air; lighting systems; dust and gaseous effluent collection and purification systems

assessment_methods.method: discussion of team works / written reports

assessment_rules: The summative assessment consists of the discussion of team works (contributing 40% to the final mark) and an oral test with two questions (contributing 60% to the final mark). To pass, students must demonstrate knowledge of basic terminology, ability to assess investment viability, develop plant sizing, apply PERT and CPM, design layout, apply holding techniques, use time and work measurement, and size auxiliary systems. Grades reflect four levels of preparation: sufficient, adequate, good, and very good.
